pll2d13c2-d1e3519.summary: Asks whether that light was corporeal or spiritual, answering from the saints.

pll2d13c2-d1e3522.summary: Cites Augustine: the light can be understood corporeally or spiritually. Spiritually it is angelic nature, first unformed ('heaven' in Gen 1:1), then formed when converted to the Creator and cleaving to him by charity ('let there be light'); it was first darkness, then light.
claims: Spiritually, the first light is angelic nature formed by conversion.

pll2d13c2-d1e3548.summary: Cites Augustine on Genesis: this creature was unformed before being formed in love of its Maker, and formed when turned to the unchangeable light of the Word.
claims: Angelic nature was formed by turning to the Word.

pll2d13c2-d1e3567.summary: Holds that if the light was corporeal, which is probable, it was a luminous body like a bright cloud, formed from preexisting matter, not from nothing, with power to shine; the first day began with it, since before light there was neither day nor night, though there was time.
claims: Corporeal light was made from preexisting matter.
Before light there was time but no day or night.

pl-l2d13c2.summary: Asks whether that light was corporeal or spiritual. With Augustine, it can be either: spiritually, it is angelic nature, first unformed ('heaven') then formed when turned to the Creator in charity, so God divided light from darkness; corporeally, which is probable, it was a luminous body like a bright cloud, made from preexisting matter, with which the first day began, since before light there was time but neither day nor night.
claims: The first light can be read as spiritual or corporeal.
Spiritually, it is angelic nature formed by conversion to God.
Corporeally, more probably, it was a luminous body made from preexisting matter.
Before light there was time but neither day nor night.
